title.narrative: Operational performance of water and wastewater SPs and RWUs improved.

description.narrative:
Although licensing is out of the control of the WSRC, However, the WSRC will forward all approved licenses to the CoM with an immediate notification to PWA. A follow-up with the CoM office will be jointly made by the council and PWA as well as the MOLG. Discussion was initiated with the MOLG to start treating the utilities as such and not as JSCs. Nevertheless, as also explained in the former chapter, the expectation is that the process of licensing by PWA will remain very slow in the coming years. Therefore, it is proposed to downscale the planning drastically.
As for the submission of the incentives program/bylaw to PWA (draft, final, updates), and based on article 24 of the water law, the council has prepared the incentives program, which was submitted and discussed with PWA (within the first quarter of program year 2). This has not been achieved within year one due to unclarity in regards to the preparation process and the roles of different parties in both the preparation and implementation phases of the program. However, due to improved clarity and better coordination on this program with PWA, the WSRC has submitted the draft in June 2023. The program itself will only be prepared once the COM endorses the related bylaw. The bylaw has covered an implementation component based on official mandate of related stakeholders.
As for water supply agreements, the council has reached out to all SPs in the West bank and the Gaza Strip to collect water supply agreements. Enough of these agreements (more than the planning) was collected for analysis. The analysis of this first batch of agreements is expected to be completed by June 2023. Out of this analysis three framework agreements will be prepared covering agreements at RWU level, the second at other SPs level and the third for bulk water supplies. An evaluation framework for agreements adherence to prevailing laws and regulation will also be prepared. ( these were all completed within the first quarter of year 2 of the program) These will be presented and discussed with and hopefully approved by PWA. The analysis will also show WSRC’s technical and legal feedback on the current agreements used by some SPs. Based on this, recommendations will be made to those SPs. The outcome of the analysis will therefore include:
1- Characteristics of current water supply agreements 2- A framework of two water supply agreements 3- A check list of issues to look at while evaluating future water supply agreements. As also explained in the former chapter, the WSRC was expecting to collect only a few agreements. However, a good number was collected so far, and the number is still increasing.
